## What you love
- Movies over TV, by a lot. TV is only about 11% of what they like.
- **Star Wars**, all of it. Every episode rated so far is a like.
- Comedy that goes big and dumb in a good way: **Knocked Up**, **The Hangover Part II**, **The Lego Movie**.
- Animation that lands emotionally: **Inside Out**, **Despicable Me 3**, **Despicable Me 4**.
- **Christopher Nolan**.
- **Matt Damon**.
- **George Lucas** and the **Star Wars** crew (**Anthony Daniels**, **Frank Oz**, **Carrie Fisher**).
- **Kristen Wiig**, **Jonah Hill** — that comedy lane.
- Sci-fi action that holds up: **The Terminator**, **Terminator 2: Judgment Day**.
- 2010s and 2000s especially, plus some 2020s.
- The 90s canon: **The Matrix**, **The Shawshank Redemption**, **Forrest Gump**, **South Park**.
- **Back to the Future**, **One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest**, **The Simpsons**.
- Crime dramas with two pros facing off: **Heat**.

## What you avoid
- Prestige drama everyone swears is a masterpiece. **The Godfather** was a meh.
- **Friends** — meh.
- **Saturday Night Live** — meh.
- **The Fifth Element** — meh.
- Long-running TV in general, mostly.

## Right now
- Later list: **Raiders of the Lost Ark**, **Pulp Fiction**, **The Dark Knight Rises**, **Sherlock**.
- Mid-series, slow going: **Breaking Bad** (season 1), **Stranger Things** (season 2), **Fleabag** (season 2).
- Pays for basically everything: Netflix, Prime, Max, Disney+, Hulu, Apple TV+, Paramount+, Peacock.

## Notes
- "I like movies."
- "the diner scene, two pros sizing each other up"

thread.text:
you're a movies guy, full stop — TV is like 12% of what you like, and the TV you do like is **South Park**, **The Simpsons**, early SNL-adjacent stuff.

the through-line: **Star Wars**, all of it. **Christopher Nolan** and **Matt Damon** on repeat (6 each), plus the whole Lucasfilm crew. comedy that goes big and dumb in a good way (**Knocked Up**, **The Hangover Part II**, **The Lego Movie**), animation that actually lands a punch (**Inside Out**, **Despicable Me 3** and **4**), and the 90s canon.

the one crime drama you lit up for is **Heat**, and your own note on it is "the diner scene, two pros sizing each other up" — that's the tell. you want two heavyweights in a room, not a slow burn about a family. which is exactly why **The Godfather** came back a meh.
